attempts.summary: Set up /srv/data on node1 as a btrfs subvolume (backed by a loop-mounted sparse image, persisted via /etc/fstab) so it is recoverable through filesystem snapshots. Populated baseline application data, took a read-only btrfs snapshot, then modified /srv/data (deleted a file, edited two others, added junk), and restored the exact pre-modification content by recreating the subvolume from the snapshot. Verified via SHA-256 hashes that restored content exactly matches the original baseline. Completed the mandatory node-restart protocol: captured boot_id/uptime baseline, rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed, and reverified that the btrfs loop mount auto-recovered via fstab with data hashes still matching baseline.
